title: Syntax Constraints Are Not Enough: Semantic Errors Dominate Diffusion LM Tool-Calling Failures

contributions.purpose: Test whether constrained decoding closes the diffusion-LM tool-calling gap (the formatting-failure hypothesis).
contributions.mechanism: Systematic controlled evaluation of three decoding conditions for LLaDA-8B on BFCL-v3: unconstrained generation, best-of-2 with AST filter, and LAVE CFG-constrained decoding with a syntax-only grammar.
contributions.evaluation: CFG raises AST parse rate 91.71%->96.67% and cuts parse failures 60% (6.76%->2.67%), but overall success improves only 0.57pp (36.19%->36.76%); best-of-2 gives +0.10pp at 2x cost.
contributions.source_quote: We conduct a systematic evaluation of CFG-constrained decoding for diffusion LM tool calling, comparing unconstrained generation, best-of-n sampling, and LAVE grammar-constrained decoding on BFCL-v3.

contributions.purpose: Identify the true dominant failure mode of diffusion LM tool calling.
contributions.mechanism: Develop an error taxonomy separating parse failures from semantic errors (wrong function, wrong arguments) and track their distribution across decoding conditions.
contributions.evaluation: Semantic errors (wrong function + wrong arguments) stay ~60% of outputs and are unaffected by grammar; wrong-function errors even rise (12.86%->15.52%). A 50.74pp gap vs Qwen-8B AR (87.5%) remains.
contributions.domain: Structured output error analysis for diffusion LMs
contributions.source_quote: We develop an error taxonomy that disentangles syntactic failures from semantic errors, revealing that semantic errors dominate (~60%) and are unaffected by grammar constraints.

contributions.purpose: Show heterogeneous, sometimes harmful, effects of grammar constraints across task categories.
contributions.mechanism: Per-category success-rate analysis across the 7 BFCL Non-Live categories comparing unconstrained vs LAVE CFG.
contributions.evaluation: CFG helps parallel calls (+7.33pp) but degrades irrelevance detection (-8.00pp, grammar forces a call when abstention is correct); Java stays near-zero across conditions.
contributions.source_quote: We analyze heterogeneous effects across task categories, finding that CFG constraints benefit parallel function calls (+7.3pp) but degrade irrelevance detection (-8.0pp).

self_declared_provenance.quote: A common hypothesis attributes this performance gap to formatting failures ... We systematically test this hypothesis by applying CFG-constrained decoding to LLaDA-8B on BFCL-v3 and analyzing the resulting error distribution.
Apply LAVE (Zhang et al., 2026) constrained decoding with a syntax-only context-free grammar that enforces valid Python call-list structure.
LAVE (Zhang et al., 2026) addresses this through a lookahead-then-verify approach that enforces context-free grammar (CFG) constraints during the diffusion process.
diffusion language models significantly underperform on these structured output tasks compared to autoregressive models of similar scale (Lu et al., 2026).

notes: Negative result on the intervention: CFG constraints improve syntactic validity but yield only +0.57pp overall success (near-tie), and grammar enforcement hurts the irrelevance category (-8pp); overall a large 50.74pp gap to AR models persists.
